rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with a 14-day written notice to quit. The tenant can stop the termination by paying all rent due, with interest and costs, on or before the answer day in an eviction case. If the delay was caused by late government subsidy payments, the court must continue the hearing at least 7 days.
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment; right to cure by paying rent due, interest and costs
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies under a written lease with unpaid rent.

parsed.doc_summary: Official text of Massachusetts G.L. c. 186, § 11, which sets a 14-day written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease, with a right to cure and a hearing continuance when government payments were delayed.
